summary:
### TL;DR
- **Notification changes start December 1, 2026.** GitHub.com is changing how notification subscriptions work, rolling out over one week. It does not apply to GitHub Enterprise Server. GitHub says no action is required. However, any email filters or automations that rely on notification reasons should be reviewed. ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-24-more-predictable-notifications-on-github-com))
- **Security advisory notifications get a clearer label.** When your team is @mentioned in a comment on a repository security advisory, the notification will now say "team mention" instead of "commented". ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-24-more-predictable-notifications-on-github-com))
- **CodeQL docs now list `codeql/actions-queries` as a core query pack** that ships with the standard CodeQL CLI bundle. ([source](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/34e9c11a32a9dd64cf9455542f77736690886440))

### Action required
No breaking changes or deprecations. One date to plan around:

- **By December 1, 2026: check notification filters and automations.** ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-24-more-predictable-notifications-on-github-com))
  - **The reason shown is now chosen by priority, not by most recent activity.** This affects both the inbox and the email footer. The priority order is:
    1. mention
    2. team mention
    3. assign
    4. review requested
    5. comment
    6. manual
    7. author
    8. state change
    9. subscribed

    For issues, assign has the highest priority.
  - **Email headers will list every reason that applies**, for example both "mention" and "subscribed".
  - **Impact:** filters that route security or CI-related mail based on a single reason value may behave differently.

### Security improvements
- **Security advisory triage.** Team @mentions in repository security advisory comments now show the reason "team mention" rather than "commented". This makes them easier to filter and route. ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-24-more-predictable-notifications-on-github-com))
- **Team mentions follow current team membership.** ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-24-more-predictable-notifications-on-github-com))
  - People who leave a team, or whose team mention is removed, stop getting future notifications based on that mention.
  - People who join a team start getting notifications for future activity on threads where the team was already mentioned.
  - This matters for security teams where membership changes.
- **Unsubscribing now sticks.** Routine activity no longer re-subscribes you after you manually unsubscribe. This includes comments, reviews, state changes, and merge queue activity. Being mentioned, assigned, or asked to review a pull request will still re-subscribe you. ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-24-more-predictable-notifications-on-github-com))

### Docs changes worth reading
- **CodeQL query packs:** `codeql/actions-queries` has been added to the documented list of core CodeQL query packs. These packs are published in the Container registry and come pre-downloaded with the CodeQL CLI bundle. In practice, this means queries for analyzing GitHub Actions workflows are now documented alongside the language packs, such as `cpp`, `csharp`, and `go`. ([page](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/code-scanning/codeql/query-packs), [commit](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/34e9c11a32a9dd64cf9455542f77736690886440))

changelog.title: More predictable notifications on GitHub.com
changelog.text: Starting December 1, 2026, we’re migrating notifications on GitHub.com over the course of a week to make subscriptions more predictable, correct unexpected behavior, and support the growing scale of activity. During the rollout, notifications may behave differently for different users. No action is required, but the changes below may affect how you manage and filter notifications. This does not apply to GitHub Enterprise Server. What is changing Routine activity won’t resubscribe you: Previously, after manually unsubscribing, notification activities such as commenting, submitting a pull request review, changing a thread’s state, or merge queue activity resulted in a re-subscription. Now, those actions leave you unsubscribed. Being mentioned, assigned, or receiving a pull request review request will continue to resubscribe you since those actions ask for your attention. Team-mention notifications will reflect current team membership and mentions: Previously, you could continue receiving notifications after a team mention was removed or you left the team. If you joined a team after it was mentioned, you wouldn’t receive notifications for future activity. Now, removing the mention or leaving the team stops future notifications based on that team mention, so you may receive fewer notifications. Joining the team enables notifications for future activity on threads where it was already mentioned. Other reasons, such as commenting, may still result in notifications. Removing a mention won’t stop notifications you receive for other reasons: Previously, removing a mention could stop notifications even if you’d also participated in another way. Now, if someone removes a mention, you’ll stay subscribed as long as another reason, such as commenting or being assigned, still applies. The Subscriptions page will show only subscriptions you added manually : The Subscriptions page will only list threads you explicitly subscribed to, not threads you get notifications for because you authored, commented, were assigned, were mentioned, or were asked to review. To manage those notifications and bulk-unsubscribe, use your notification inbox . Notification reasons will follow a consistent priority: The reason shown in your inbox and email footer is now based on priority instead of the most recent activity. The order is mention, team mention, assign, review requested, comment, manual, author, state change, and subscribed. For issues, assign has the highest priority. If you filter or automate based on notification reasons, review those rules, since the reason shown may change. Email headers will include all notification reasons: Notification email headers will include all applicable notification reasons, such as “mention” and “subscribed”, helping you better filter notifications. If you use filters or automations based on these notification reasons, please review them as they will now include all notification reasons. Team mentions in security advisory comments will show a “team mention” reason: If your team is @mentioned in a comment on a repository security advisory, the notification will say “team mention” instead of “commented”. Other notification behaviors, such as notification settings, watched repositories, custom thread subscriptions, and previously delivered notifications remain unchanged. Join the discussion in GitHub Community . The post More predictable notifications on GitHub.com appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
